home.title: collage — Go sites and web apps, no client framework
home.description: A Go framework for server-rendered sites and web apps: HTML from fragments, cached by what it depends on, extended by plugins. No client framework.
home.eyebrow: A Go framework for the server-rendered web
home.headline: Your site doesn't need a <mark>client framework</mark>.
home.tagline: HTML already does most of the work, and a few lines of plain JavaScript do the rest. collage renders pages on the server from fragments, sends only the part that changed when something does, and ships as one Go binary.

why.title: A landing page is not a single-page app
why.text: A product page, a landing page, a site of a few pages with little to click: none of them needs a JavaScript server runtime, a client framework and a hydration step. Such a runtime is slower than Go and keeps more memory and disk busy on the server, and a client framework sends the browser a program to build the HTML it could have received. collage sends the HTML.

d.label: A typical stack — a JavaScript bundle, hydration, an SSR framework, a dependency tree and a JavaScript runtime — beside collage: HTML, a few lines of JavaScript and one Go binary.

fragments.title: Fragments, not components
fragments.text: A page is a layout around fragments. Each fragment is a template and a function that fetches its own data; siblings fetch at once, and the page still comes out in order. Open one at a URL of its own with WithFragmentPath, and three lines of fetch replace just that part of the page: the server's state, rendered on the server, one fragment at a time.
fragments.note: fetch, XHR, server-sent events and WebSockets were made for exactly this. When you would rather not write the script, a plugin refreshes fragments on an interval or when the server pushes, and can morph them in place.

cache.title: Cached by what it depends on
cache.text: Every page and every cached value carries the tags of what it was built from: post:hello, author:ada. InvalidateTags marks the pages that used a tag stale and renders them again in the background, keeping the old page to fall back on. PurgeTags removes them outright, for what must never be shown again. Everything else stays cached.

plugins.title: Middleware and plugins, as many as you need
plugins.text: Where a framework gives you one middleware file and every concern a request needs is chained inside it by hand, collage's app.Use takes any func(http.Handler) http.Handler, as many times as you like, and each plugin brings its own middleware, in the order you list them. The core stays small: sessions, spam protection, live updates, SEO and metrics are plugins. Forty-four are published, and one of your own is a Go type with the hooks it needs.
plugins.all: Every plugin, and how to write one

go.title: Still Go
go.text: There is no second language and no second process. Your data layer is your Go code: the database, the queue, the external API. An API or a service you already have mounts on collage's own mux with app.Handle, beside the pages and behind the same middleware. One project, one binary.

apps.title: A small core, for sites and web apps
apps.text: collage is not batteries-included, and it says what it leaves to you. What it has is what a server-rendered front end needs, so a multi-user, role-based web app is as much at home as a landing page: sessions and roles, forms that cannot be forged, spam protection, parts of the page that update live.

layouts.title: Layouts and slots
layouts.text: A layout leaves a slot for the page's content, and a fragment can leave slots of its own. Fill them with fragments and collage assembles the page.

invalidate.title: Invalidate by tag
invalidate.text: A page remembers what it was built from. Invalidate one tag and only the pages that used it are rendered again; the rest stay as they are.

fetch.title: Fetch at once
fetch.text: Every fragment has its own data handler. Sibling fragments fetch together, and the HTML still comes out in order.

live.title: Stream fragments live
live.text: With collage-live, invalidating a tag re-renders every open fragment that used it and pushes it to the browser over one stream. Only that part changes. For example CPU usage of the server here.

dev.title: Save and see
dev.text: collage dev reloads the browser when a template changes and rebuilds when Go does. A failed render shows its file and line in the browser.

build.title: Build, export, serve
build.text: collage build makes one static binary, the site's whole server, for any operating system and architecture. collage export writes the site as static files, and collage serve serves them the way a static host would.
